item.title: CDC funding for HIV prevention shifted from providers to states under Trump
item.description: Nonprofits fighting HIV used get direct funding from the CDC. Now that money is going to state health departments that may have other priorities.

item.title: An early start to flu season moves up vaccination timing
item.description: This year's flu season is unusual. It started early and in the West, instead of the South. A new variant with a mutation that helps the virus evade immunity may be playing a role.
item.content:encoded: This year's flu season is unusual. It started early and in the West, instead of the South. A new variant with a mutation that helps the virus evade immunity may be playing a role.

item.title: What happened during Christa Pike's failed execution
item.description: Catherine Sweeney was in the witness room when Tennessee attempted to execute Christa Pike on Sept. 30. An attempted execution in May had also failed. Here's what Sweeney saw and heard.

item.title: Wildfire smoke affects animals in unique ways. Scientists are trying to understand it
item.description: The new field of "smoke ecology" examines how wildfire smoke perturbs wild places and animals — and what might be done to prevent its worst mayhem.

item.title: From floating saunas to clinical trials: How heat might help mental health
item.description: While scientists have a decent understanding of how sauna and other forms of heat exposure exercises our cardiovascular system, they know relatively little about its impact on mental health.

item.title: Heat-related deaths in Phoenix rise, after two years of decline
item.description: Metro Phoenix has so far seen twice as many heat deaths as this time last year. Authorities are trying to understand why and how to intervene.
